text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: P95/P99 latency alert for /v1/generate on model-redwood-3a in eu-west-1. p95 ~ 620ms (SLO 200ms), p99 ~ 3.2s. paging oncall @alex_oncall.

alex_oncall: saw it, I'm paged. starting triage. any customer pages?

samira: small spike started ~1823456000, correlates with a rollout of continuous-batcher v1.9 canary on a subset of pods. streaming stalls and tail increase on the batching path.

nate: confirming: tail traces show queuing in batch-scheduler task loop, lots of small + very large seqlen mixes causing head-of-line.

alex_oncall: timeline: when did canary start?

samira: canary deploy at 1823455500, 10% of serving pool. metrics stayed fine then ramped.

maya: customer impact: one enterprise tenant reported intermittent 5s responses on streaming websockets, ~2% of requests affected. CS notified.

alex_oncall: ok mitigation plan: 1) throttle batcher -> reduce max_batch_size, 2) enable fairshare scheduling between short/long sequences, 3) fallback to non-batched path for streaming until stabilized. I'll run steps and update.

nate: suggest immediate change: set `batcher.max_batch_size=8` -> `4` on canary nodes and flip scheduling weight for long sequences to 0.3. Also enable `batcher.enable_streaming_low_latency=true`.

alex_oncall: running command to patch config on canary group:

```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/continuous-batcher CANARY=true BATCHER_MAX=4 FAIR_LONG_WEIGHT=0.3
```

alex_oncall: applied to canary group. watching metrics.

(2m later)

incident-bot: config change detected for deploy/continuous-batcher (canary) at 1823456600.

samira: p95 dropped to ~240ms on canary, p99 down to ~900ms. global still high because canary autoscaled and spillover happened.

alex_oncall: next: enable streaming fallback route on edge for affected route -> route to non-batched streaming pool.

nate: patch gateway rule: `route /v1/generate streaming -> streaming-pool-v2 if header x-fallback=on or response-latency>800ms`. applying.

```
kubectl -n gateway apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  streaming-fallback: |
    rules:
      - path: /v1/generate
        condition: latency>800
        target: streaming-pool-v2
EOF
```

alex_oncall: gateway change applied 1823456800. streaming errors dropped, customer report from CS says fewer hits.

maya: CS: affected tenant report: 80% of their requests back to normal, will monitor.

samira: observed a secondary issue: the scheduler's batching queue wasn't honoring per-model isolation when one model sent many mixed-length requests; added per-model queue cap to avoid cross-model head-of-line.

nate: I've pushed a hotfix to batch-scheduler: `enforceQueueIsolation=true, maxInflightPerModel=50` and bumped kv-cache warmup. Redeploying to canary.

(4m later)

incident-bot: deploy batch-scheduler v1.9.1 to canary at 1823456900 succeeded.

samira: canary p99 now ~520ms, global p99 trending down. p95 back within SLO for most routes.

alex_oncall: decision: hold canary rollback? we should keep fixes and gradually roll forward but keep max_batch_size lowered and fairshare enabled cluster-wide until we validate. I'll coord with release owner.

maya: logged customer impact summary to #customer-impact and notified account team.

nate: follow-up items checked into runbook: 1) add automated detection for mixed-seqlen spikes, 2) add canary knob to auto-lower batch size on latency jitter, 3) create a dashboard for per-model queue occupancy.

alex_oncall: handing off to @samira for overnight watch. key facts in this thread. next oncall, please monitor p95/p99, streaming stalls, and KV-cache hitrate.

samira: taking handoff. brief: cause continuous-batcher scheduling + mixed sequence lengths -> tail queuing. mitigations applied: reduce batch size on canary & global hold, enable fairshare, per-model queue isolation, streaming fallback route, batch-scheduler hotfix.

sre-runbook-bot: handoff checklist completed by samira at 1823456950. :white_check_mark:

alex_oncall: thanks team. will follow up with postmortem draft tomorrow and coordinate permanent perf improvements. :thumbsup:
